The '''2016–17 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team''' represented [[Vanderbilt University]] in the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. This was [[Bryce Drew]]'s first year as the Vanderbilt head coach. The Commodores played their home games at [[Memorial Gymnasium (Vanderbilt University)|Memorial Gymnasium]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee]] as members of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. They finished the season 19–16, 10–8 in [[2016–17 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fifth place. They defeated [[2016–17 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] and [[2016–17 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the [[2017 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] before losing in the semifinals to [[2016–17 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the First Round to [[2016-17 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]]. Vanderbilt entered the NCAA Tournament with 15 losses, the most ever by any at-large team.<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/the-latest-late-tournament-titles-dont-effect-bracket-much/2017/03/12/b9fae6f8-0767-11e7-bd19-fd3afa0f7e2a_story.html The Washington Post]{{dead link|date=June 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2015–16 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Commodores]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] 19–14, 11–7 in [[2015–16 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for third place. They lost in the second round of the [[2016 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] to [[2015–16 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the First Four to [[2015–16 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]].

On March 27, 2016, head coach [[Kevin Stallings]] resigned to become the head coach at [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2016/03/27/Sources-say-Vanderbilt-s-Kevin-Stallings-offered-Pitt-men-s-basketball-job/stories/201603270181|title = Vanderbilt's Kevin Stallings hired as Pitt men's basketball coach}}</ref> Shortly thereafter, the school hired Valparaiso head coach Bryce Drew as head coach.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/15140517/vanderbilt-commodores-hire-bryce-drew-valparaiso-crusaders-new-coach|title=Vandy hires coach Bryce Drew from Valparaiso|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-08-15}}</ref>
